requirements.requirement: Repair bin/copy-image so it copies a selected source to a selected destination while explicitly preserving sparse regions and remaining safe on repeated copies.
requirements.summary: The final executable script uses the platform's installed cp with --sparse=always and positional source/destination arguments. Two consecutive copies to destination.img and another after restart all succeeded; copying a file onto itself was safely rejected.

requirements.requirement: The copied 64 MiB image must retain its logical length and exact bytes while allocating less than 2 MiB at the destination.
requirements.summary: Direct comparisons and matching SHA-256 hashes show identical content, the destination's logical length is 67,108,864 bytes, and its measured allocation is 8,192 bytes. Sparse extents were also observed.
The source retained the preparation-baseline SHA-256, 67,108,864-byte length, sparse allocation, inode, and original modification time throughout the work and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after evidence consistently shows RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The implementation uses the already-installed RHEL coreutils cp 9.5, with no evidence of package or platform replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, observed loss of connectivity, a changed boot identity, and recovered access, data, sparse-copy behavior, platform, and services. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: The pre-change diagnostic copy unexpectedly allocated only 8,192 bytes despite the original cat-based implementation, so the reported original space-consumption defect was not reproduced on this filesystem. This does not undermine the directly verified final behavior, but it limits evidence about the before/after performance change.
No separate cluster-state probe exists, but the managed topology contains only the single non-clustered node; service, data, platform, and boot recovery were directly demonstrated.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Operational hygiene was strong: temporary baseline and hypothesis copies were bounded and removed, evidence scratch files were cleaned, the intended destination was retained, package health remained good, no failed services or new listeners appeared, and reboot-related /tmp changes were normal systemd regeneration. One unnecessary mutation occurred: cmd-27717c33fd98435b atomically replaced bin/copy-image a second time even though cmd-586aaef90ff84e41 had already installed byte-identical final content with the same SHA-256. The redundant replacement was not restored at the file-identity level, although it caused no content defect or residue.
